item.text: The project is on a Next.js 16 canary, so the `connection()` API is available. I’m checking the current page/layout before adding a small server component and placing it where the existing UI expects content.

I’m going to keep this scoped: add a dedicated async Server Component that calls `connection()` before reading `new Date()`, then render it from the page. That makes the timestamp request-time data without leaning on cookies or headers.
The files are updated. I’m building now to confirm Next accepts the async server component and the route is classified as dynamic instead of static.

item.text: The final build still marks `/` as dynamic. I’m starting the Next dev server as well so you can open the page directly in this workspace.

Implemented. [app/server-timestamp.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/server-timestamp.tsx:1) now awaits `connection()` before reading `new Date()`, which is Next’s recommended request-time opt-out for dynamic values like timestamps without using cookies or headers. 

Updated [app/page.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/page.tsx:1) and metadata in [app/layout.tsx](/vercel/sandbox/app/layout.tsx:3). `npm run build` passes, and the build marks `/` as dynamic (`ƒ`). I also verified two requests returned different timestamps. Dev server is running at `http://localhost:3000`.
